title: DeadDrop OSCORE identity ignores live security_context
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: correctness (security impact on POST gate and private ACL)

Spec 18.9: writes MUST be OSCORE-protected; rate limits and private/group ACL are per OSCORE context. _request_context_id() / _bound_oscore_identity() only accept request.oscore_context, request.oscore_context_id, and the same names on request.remote. Strings, non-empty bytes, or durable_context_id() count.

The live aiocoap stack does not set those attributes. After successful unprotect, request.remote is aiocoap.transports.oscore.OSCOREAddress(security_context, underlying_address). ConfessionsResource already reads recipient_id/kid on the context object.

Evidence:
- _request_context_id never reads remote.security_context or recipient_id (deaddrop.py ~59-98).
- python/tests/coap/test_deaddrop_resource.py _protected() sets request.oscore_context_id by hand. Stack tests only cover unprotected and spoofed option -> 4.01; there is no live unprotect POST that succeeds.
- lichen.crypto.oscore.MemorySecurityContext.durable_context_id() is _sender_context_id(), which hashes master_secret+salt+id_context+sender_id and omits recipient_id. If oscore_context were the live MemorySecurityContext, every pairwise peer would share one rate-limit and private-drop ACL.

This is not a refile of worker6-ex47 (spoofed option-as-auth, fixed). After that fix the gate still cannot see the identity the stack actually binds, so legitimate OSCORE POSTs return 4.01 oscore_required, and wiring durable_context_id() naively would collapse peers.

Impact:
- Python /deaddrop cannot accept real OSCORE writes on the live stack.
- Private/group ACL and 6/hour quota cannot be per-peer even if the attribute were later set to MemorySecurityContext.

Oracle: ConfessionsResource recipient_id/kid; aiocoap OSCOREAddress.security_context after unprotect.
acceptance_criteria: A request unprotected by the live stack (request.remote is aiocoap OSCOREAddress with security_context, or MemorySecurityContext) is accepted for POST, rate-limited per peer recipient_id, and used as the private/group ACL key. Two pairwise peers must not share a bucket. Spoofed opt.oscore still returns 4.01. Tests must drive a real post-unprotect remote, not only request.oscore_context_id.
close_reason: Bound DeadDrop authorization, private/group ACL, and per-peer quota state to the live post-unprotect remote.security_context recipient_id/KID, preferring authenticated peer identity over local sender/durable context IDs and failing closed when live peer identity is absent. Added live MemorySecurityContext regressions for peer role, durable-ID collision/per-peer buckets, reconstructed-context quota replay, spoof fallback, missing identity, and private ACL isolation. 140 focused DeadDrop/secure CoAP/OSCORE tests, Ruff lint/format, scoped strict mypy, and diff check pass.
